chunks: And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) both narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah the Exalted assigned to al-Husayn (peace be upon him) seventy thousand angels who send blessings upon him every day, disheveled and covered with dust, from the day he was killed until what Allah wills, meaning the rising of the Qa'im (peace be upon him).

key_terms.قِيَامَ الْقَائِمِ: the rising of the Qa'im (the Twelfth Imam)

ai.seo_question: How many angels bless Imam Husayn (a.s.) and what is their state?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cosmic significance of the Battle of Karbala, portraying the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) as an event that engaged the entire celestial hierarchy. The description of the seventy thousand angels as 'disheveled and covered in dust' (shu'than ghubran) signifies their active, humble participation in mourning, a state of perpetual devotion that bridges the earthly sacrifice with the eschatological expectation of the Qa'im (a.s.).

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 5. My father and ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain both narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥakam, from ‘Ali ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Basīr, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: Allāh has dedicated seventy thousand angels to Ḥusain (a.s.) who are disheveled and covered with dust; they send blessings on him everyday since the day he was killed (and will continue to do so) until (a time) which only Allāh knows – referring to the rising of the Qā`im (a.s.).
